question: Should OpenClaw expose a permanent plugin SDK capability that lets external plugins emit manifest-authorized AI-safety events into the durable, operator-facing safety timeline?
rationale: This is a new public API and manifest policy with security semantics; source review can verify mechanics and provenance stamping but cannot decide whether that product contract belongs in core or what long-term trust and retention guarantees OpenClaw should make.

options.title: Approve a bounded public contract
options.body: Approve the manifest-gated emitter with explicit documentation of untrusted provenance, allowed metadata, retention, and compatibility expectations before merge.

options.title: Keep the taxonomy core-only
options.body: Restrict emission to core and bundled components for now, deferring any external plugin API until the permanent contract is designed.

options.title: Move the plugin capability to a follow-up
options.body: Land only a maintainer-approved internal observability foundation, while tracking the external-plugin contract separately.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded public contract
recommendation.body: Approve the manifest-gated emitter with explicit documentation of untrusted provenance, allowed metadata, retention, and compatibility expectations before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available review context identifies the feature-series author but does not expose a verified current-main diagnostics or plugin-SDK owner; a repository owner should make the final decision.
